metaTitle: Best Backlit Large Print Keyboards in 2026
metaDescription: Six backlit large print keyboards compared on backlight type, connection, wrist support and noise, for comfortable typing in dim rooms and at night.
introParagraphs: A large print keyboard solves half the problem, and a backlight solves the other half when the room is dim or the evening is long. The challenge is that many backlit boards pair large legends with flashy rainbow lighting that is more distracting than helpful. This guide compares six that handle both jobs, from the TECURS with a steady white LED and seven brightness levels to the Atelus with a rainbow backlight and the OMOTON with a calm white glow.

The six differ in connection and lighting style. The TECURS and OMOTON offer a dual USB and Type-C connector for old and new computers, the HeengYanson adds a wrist rest with soft-touch keys, and the KOPJIPPOM is a wireless combo with seven colors and one USB plug for keyboard and mouse. The EDJO takes a different path, with retro round keys and a typewriter look.

We evaluated each keyboard from product specs and buyer feedback, concentrating on how easy the backlight is to control and how readable the legends stay when lit. For most readers, a steady white or warm backlight is easier on aging eyes than a rainbow cycle. Choose the style you can set once and forget.

products.name: TECURS Large Print Backlit Keyboard
products.description:
The TECURS is the best overall backlit pick because it keeps the lighting calm and the setup flexible. A bright, evenly distributed white LED backlight lights the oversized legends, which are claimed to be four times larger than standard. It offers seven adjustable brightness levels, so you can fine tune the glow for the room.

The 2-in-1 connector supports both USB and Type C, so the same keyboard works with older desktops and newer laptops. Dedicated multimedia keys give quick access to volume and playback, which is handy for video calls. The tradeoff is that it has a single backlight color, so anyone who wants colors will prefer the HeengYanson or KOPJIPPOM.

Ownership is simple, with a wired plug and no batteries. Choose it over the OMOTON if you want more brightness steps and the media keys.
products.bestFor: Evening typists who want a steady white light and flexible plugs
pros: Even white backlight with seven brightness levels
USB and Type C in one connector
Dedicated multimedia keys for volume and playback
Silent full-size layout
cons: Wired cable limits how far you can move it

products.description:
The OMOTON pairs oversize font keys with a soft white backlight, which the listing says reduces eye fatigue during long work. It carries both a USB C and a USB A connector, so it works with older PCs and newer laptops without an adapter. The letters are claimed to be four times larger than standard.

The white light is gentle, and that suits readers who find colored LEDs busy. The tradeoff is a connector quirk: if you use the USB A interface, the Type C end must stay plugged into the keyboard, so setup takes one extra look at the instructions. It also offers fewer backlight levels than the TECURS.

Compared with the HeengYanson, it lacks the wrist rest and color options. Choose it for a bedroom desk where calm light is the priority.
products.bestFor: Calm, single-color light with both old and new ports

cons: Connector setup needs a careful read of the note
No wrist rest or color options

products.name: HeengYanson Large Print Backlit Keyboard with Wrist Rest
products.description:
The HeengYanson stands out for including a wrist rest and soft-touch keys for long typing. The silent keys reduce noise, and the large print legends are lit by a seven-color backlight with adjustable brightness. It designed for hours at the desk, which is a clear advantage over the lighter boards.

The tradeoff is that colorful backlights can distract, so pick a steady color. A wrist rest also adds depth, and some users find the pad too tall.

Ownership is easy, with USB plug and play. Compared with the TECURS, it adds the wrist rest and colors but lacks the dual connector. Choose it if you type for long sessions and want the comfort built in.
products.bestFor: Long typing sessions where wrist comfort matters
pros: Wrist rest included for long sessions
Soft-touch keys are quiet
Seven colors with adjustable brightness
Simple USB plug and play
cons: Wrist rest adds depth on a small desk
Colors can distract if not set steady

products.name: Atelus Large Print Backlit Keyboard
products.description:
The Atelus is for readers who actually like colorful lighting. The rainbow backlight illuminates the keys for typing at night, and the legends are claimed to be four times larger than standard. A full-size layout and plug and play setup keep it easy to use.

The tradeoff is that a rainbow backlight is the least calm choice here, and flashing or color changing effects can disorient light-sensitive users. It also has no wrist rest.

Setup needs no drivers. Compared with the TECURS, it offers color but fewer brightness steps. Choose it only if you enjoy color and can set a steady mode.

cons: Rainbow lighting can distract or disorient

products.name: KOPJIPPOM Large Print Wireless Keyboard and Mouse
products.description:
The KOPJIPPOM is the only wireless set in this guide, pairing a backlit large print keyboard with a mouse. One USB receiver serves both, and the receiver sits on the back of the keyboard with an indicator bar so it is hard to lose. A seven-color backlight with adjustable brightness lights the oversize letters.

The wireless link frees the desk of cables, and the combo covers Windows and Mac OS. The tradeoff is that a backlit wireless board draws battery power, so expect to recharge or replace batteries.

Setup is quick. Compared with the wired TECURS, you get a mouse and a cleaner desk, but add a battery chore. Choose it if you want a matched pair.

pros: Keyboard and mouse share one USB receiver

Works with Windows and Mac

products.name: EDJO Large Print Retro Round Key Keyboard
products.description:
The EDJO blends vintage looks with modern function, featuring round keycaps in a typewriter style. The oversize legends are claimed to be four times larger than standard, and a seven-color backlight offers three brightness levels. It is the lowest-cost pick in the guide.

Round keys have a distinctive feel, and some users like the clear separation between keys. The tradeoff is that round keycaps present a smaller target than flat ones and can feel unfamiliar after years on a standard board. The compact body may also lack a numeric keypad.

It connects by USB. Compared with the OMOTON, it adds a retro look at a lower cost. Choose it for style, or as a second keyboard.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A steady white or warm backlight is easier on aging eyes than a rainbow cycle. The TECURS and OMOTON offer calm white light, while the Atelus uses rainbow lighting. Flashing or color-changing effects can disorient light-sensitive users. Choose the style you can set once and forget.

Backlighting needs adjustable brightness to avoid glare. The TECURS has seven brightness levels, the EDJO three, and the HeengYanson adjustable brightness. More steps let you match the room. Some models reset to a default color at power-up, so check feedback.

Newer laptops often have only Type C, and older desktops use USB A. The TECURS has a 2-in-1 USB plus Type C connector, and the OMOTON has dual USB C and USB A. For the OMOTON, the Type C end must stay plugged in when you use USB A. Check your port before buying.

The four-times-larger claim is common and unverified, and one guide suggests the real range is 2x to 4x. Compare key dimensions and contrast instead. A lit legend on a dark key reads better in the dark, while bright rooms need strong contrast. Large print is a start, not a guarantee.

The HeengYanson includes a wrist rest and soft-touch keys, and the TECURS offers silent typing. Slightly spaced keys can reduce accidental double presses for arthritic hands. A tall wrist pad can push wrists upward, so check the fit. Try a board in person if possible.

Wired boards avoid battery concerns, while wireless uses a USB receiver or Bluetooth. The KOPJIPPOM combo shares one receiver for keyboard and mouse. Backlit wireless boards drain batteries faster. Choose wired for simplicity.

howWeEvaluated.title: Backlight quality
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared color options, brightness steps and the calmness of each light. The TECURS with seven brightness levels led, and the Atelus rainbow lighting ranked lower for distraction. Steady light scored higher than effects.

howWeEvaluated.title: Legend readability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at print size claims, key color and lit contrast. All boards claim four times larger print, so we treated that as marketing. Contrast and backlight evenness mattered more.

howWeEvaluated.title: Connectivity
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked connector types and wireless options. The TECURS and OMOTON have dual connectors, and the KOPJIPPOM is wireless. Flexible connectors scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Comfort
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated wrist rests, key feel and noise from specs and buyer feedback. The HeengYanson led on wrist support and the EDJO has quiet round keys. Comfort matters for evening sessions.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value
howWeEvaluated.description: The EDJO is the lowest cost and the KOPJIPPOM combo the highest.

faq.q: How do I choose between white and colored backlights?
faq.a: White is calmer and distracts less, which suits most older eyes. Colors add style and can help if one hue reads better for you. The TECURS and OMOTON use white, while the HeengYanson and Atelus offer colors.

faq.q: Are backlit keyboards worth the extra cost?
faq.a: If you type in dim rooms, yes. The backlight lets you see the legends without turning on a bright lamp. In a bright room, high contrast may be enough.
LED backlights usually last for years, but verified buyer feedback is the best guide for each model. Some models may reset color or brightness at power-up. Avoid heavy pressure on the keys.

faq.q: Is rainbow lighting safe for sensitive eyes?
faq.a: Steady colors are fine, but flashing or cycling effects can disorient light-sensitive users. If you buy the Atelus, choose one color and leave it. A white light is safer.
Check your computer first. The TECURS and OMOTON cover both USB and Type C. If you only have USB A, any wired board works.

faq.q: Do backlit boards use more power?
faq.a: Wired boards draw power from the computer, so there is no battery to manage. Wireless backlit boards like the KOPJIPPOM combo drain batteries faster. Turn the backlight off when you do not need it.
